items.component: client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/ShadowReview.tsx (lazy-loaded at surfaceViews.ts:343, registered at surfaceViews.ts:567 as { component: ShadowReview, full: true }); no mdx/pdev delegation
items.does: Read-only. It shows the newest completed shadow-review run for each of the five reviewer lenses across the whole organisation, with that run's recorded RTF/CRL gate scores and findings. A person can switch lenses (ShadowReview.tsx:274-281). It cannot start a review: 'Re-run this reviewer' only sends a prompt to AnA (ShadowReview.tsx:385-390, which the code itself flags as a mock action), and 'Open the sequence' navigates to ectd-coauthor (ShadowReview.tsx:391).
items.backend: Only one data call: useLiveRows('/api/shadow-review') at ShadowReview.tsx:81. It is served by server/routes/shadow-review.routes.ts:35-48 through assembleOrgShadowReview (server/services/shadow-review/shadow-review-view-assembler.ts:50-104). That function runs SELECT DISTINCT ON (lens) over shadow_review_runs and shadow_review_findings, scoped by org only, not by sequence. The route is mounted at register-inline-routes.ts:1018 (mountAll with authMiddleware). That file is reached from registerInlineAiWorkflowRoutes, which server/startup/routes.ts:173 calls. Both tables are created by migrations/20260604_shadow_review.sql:12-48, which is on the apply path (scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:113, inside C2C_MIGRATION_FILES at :86). The legacy blob table c2c_shadow_review (db/migrations/20260717_shadow_review_store.sql) is marked deprecated and nothing reads it. Rows are written only by runShadowReview (shadow-review-service.ts:177-253). Two things call it: POST /api/submissions/sequences/:seqId/shadow-review (server/routes/submissions.ts:1151, mounted at register-governance-routes.ts:65) and the AnA tool run_shadow_review (AnaToolExecutor.ts:9750). The run needs the AI gateway. docs/evidence/DEMO/biotech/README.md:99 records HTTP 502 and a failed run row when no provider is configured. Production is blocked twice. (1) The surface is not in LAUNCH_APPS or LAUNCH_SHELL_SURFACES (shared/constants/launch-scope.ts:44-159), so applyLaunchScope locks it (navigation-entitlements.ts:265-285), and enforcement is on when unset in production (launch-scope.ts:43-45). (2) No surface's apiPrefixes claims /api/shadow-review: the registry lists only '/api/submissions/sequences' (ui-surface-registry.ui-v2.ts:164). So launchScopeApiVerdict returns 'unmapped' (launch-scope-api.ts:100), which is refused in production, and the D2 inventory files this namespace under 'unmapped' (docs/evidence/D2-API-SCOPE/2026-09-25/stage3-route-inventory.json:2396).

items.gaps: 1. It cannot run a review. The run button is an AnA prompt, explicitly flagged as a mock action (ShadowReview.tsx:385-387). 2. The read is not tied to any sequence or program. The assembler takes the newest completed run per lens across all of the org's sequences (shadow-review-view-assembler.ts:52-57), but the screen says 'on your connected sequence' (ShadowReview.tsx:251) and never names which sequence or submission a run belongs to. In an org with more than one sequence, it shows lens results from different sequences side by side as if they were one submission. 3. Findings cannot be acknowledged, accepted or waived here. finding.status is not even read (assembler :68-70). 4. In production both the surface and its only API path are refused by launch scope, and /api/shadow-review is attributed to no surface, so a flag flip would still leave the read returning 403. 5. Only completed runs show. Running or failed runs are invisible here, while the canonical workspace shows them.
items.duplicates: The canonical home is the Submission Center 'shadow-review' per-sequence workspace: ShadowReviewWorkspace (client/src/concept2cure/v2/surfaces/SubmissionSeqWorkspaces.tsx:831-945, rendered at SubmissionCenter.tsx:1436, with workspace ids at :336). It is in launch scope (launch-scope.ts:85-92, submission-center), and it does the whole job against the same tables. It picks a lens, POSTs /api/submissions/sequences/:seqId/shadow-review to run the review (:874-905), lists runs with running/complete/failed status (:834-835), and reads findings including their open/accepted/fixed/waived status through /api/submissions/shadow-review/:runId/findings (:839). The dispatch-readiness gate also consumes the results (registry notes at ui-surface-registry.ui-v2.ts:153). This standalone surface is an org-wide, read-only, sequence-blind second view of the same data. Recommendation: scrap it, or fold its lens-switcher presentation into the Submission Center workspace.

check.reason: I opened the files and every load-bearing claim holds. That route is server/routes/shadow-review.routes.ts:35-49 → assembleOrgShadowReview (shadow-review-view-assembler.ts:50-104), which selects DISTINCT ON (lens) from shadow_review_runs WHERE organization_id=$1 AND status='complete', with no sequence filter (:52-57). It is mounted at register-inline-routes.ts:1018 under authMiddleware and reached from server/startup/routes.ts:173. The table migration is on the apply path (scripts/db/migration-set.mjs:113). The fixture import is only the lens catalog: the 'Sample sequence' and 'Sample findings' sections of fixtures/shadow-review-data.ts:113-116 are empty. I tried to break the duplicate verdict three ways. (1) A distinct job? No. The surface cannot start a run: 'Re-run this reviewer' only calls ask() (ShadowReview.tsx:388), and the code marks it 'FLAG (mock action)' (:385-387). AnA's run_shadow_review tool exists (server/services/ana/AnaToolExecutor.ts:9750-9769), but it requires a numeric sequence_id (:9754-9757), and this surface publishes none to AnA. Its anaContext facts carry lens, runId and findings but no sequence (ShadowReview.tsx:168-208). So the prompt depends on AnA finding a sequence elsewhere. There is no acknowledge or waive action. The copy says 'on your connected sequence' (:251), but no sequence is ever identified, so lens results from different sequences can sit side by side. (2) Reachable in production? No. 'shadow-review' is in the 'Review & govern' rail group (registryModel.ts:690) and is not in NAV_HIDDEN. But it is absent from LAUNCH_APPS and LAUNCH_SHELL_SURFACES (shared/constants/launch-scope.ts:44-162), so applyLaunchScope locks it (navigation-entitlements.ts:265-284). The registry gives it only apiPrefixes ['/api/submissions/sequences'] (shared/constants/ui-surface-registry.ui-v2.ts:164), so nothing claims /api/shadow-review. launchScopeApiVerdict therefore returns 'unmapped' (launch-scope-api.ts:100), and the D2 inventory files /api/shadow-review under 'unmapped' (stage3-route-inventory.json, unmapped[198], near :2396). (3) Is the canonical home real? Yes. ShadowReviewWorkspace (SubmissionSeqWorkspaces.tsx:831-905) reads runs per sequence through GET /api/submissions/sequences/:seqId/shadow-review and findings through GET /api/submissions/shadow-review/:runId/findings (:834-843). It runs reviews via POST /api/submissions/sequences/:seqId/shadow-review (:873-879). Those routes are submissions.ts:1151/1164/1175, mounted at register-governance-routes.ts:65. The workspace is rendered at SubmissionCenter.tsx:1436 (workspace ids at :336), inside the launch-scope Submission Center app (launch-scope.ts:85-92). The standalone surface is an org-wide, read-only, sequence-blind second view of the same tables. Canonical: SubmissionCenter's ShadowReviewWorkspace.
